glossary.title: Words explained
glossary.intro: The words this dashboard and Discord use, in plain English. Something missing? Ask in the support server.

server.text: Your Discord community. Mewvo works in every server it is added to, and each server has its own settings.

channel.text: A place to talk inside the server, like #general. Text channels hold messages, voice channels hold calls.

category.text: A folder that groups channels in the channel list. Mewvo puts tickets and appeals in their own categories.

thread.text: A short side conversation that hangs off one message in a channel.

role.text: A label you give members, like "Moderator" or "Level 10". Roles decide what members can see and do, and can give a name colour.

permission.text: One thing a role allows, like "Manage Messages" or "Ban Members". Channels can change permissions for a role.

administrator.text: The permission that allows everything. In Mewvo, only people with it can change settings or punish members.

dm.text: A direct message: a private chat between two people, or between a member and Mewvo. Members can turn DMs from servers off.

mention.text: A name with @ in front, like @Sam. It sends that person a notification. Mewvo never mentions @everyone from text people type.

slashCommand.text: A command you start by typing / in the message box, like /rank. Discord shows a list as you type.

embed.text: A message box with a coloured edge, a bold title and text. Bots use them for tidy messages.

id.text: A long number Discord gives every server, channel, role and person. Turn on Developer Mode in Discord (Settings, Advanced), then right-click something and choose Copy ID.

warn.text: A written warning. The member gets a DM. Three warnings lead to a ban by themselves (see warn ladder).

mute.text: The member stays in the server but cannot write or talk, for a set time. Mewvo does this with a "Muted" role.

timeout.text: Discord's own short mute, at most 28 days. Mewvo's mute uses a role instead, so it can last longer.

kick.text: Removes the member from the server. They can come back with an invite. Mewvo sends them a new invite.

ban.text: Removes the member and stops them from coming back, for a set time or for good.

case.text: The record of one warning, mute, kick or ban: who, why, when and by whom.

caseCode.text: A short code like "k7fq2" that names one case. Members use it when they appeal.

warnLadder.text: What happens as warnings add up: warning 3 is a 7-day ban, the next one after that is 30 days, then a permanent ban.

appeal.text: A member asking staff to lift or shorten a punishment. Staff accept or deny it.

automod.text: Mewvo checking messages by itself and removing spam, bad words, invite links and raids.

reviewCard.text: A short message Mewvo posts for staff when automod does something, with buttons to keep it or undo it.

raid.text: Many new accounts joining at once to spam. When Mewvo sees one, it can make joining harder for a while (a lockdown).

modLog.text: A staff-only channel where Mewvo writes down every punishment, so everyone can look back later.

auditLog.text: A list of every change made on this dashboard: who changed which setting, and when.

removeCase.text: For a case given by mistake. Mewvo lifts what is still in effect, DMs the member, and the case stops counting. It stays on record, marked "Removed". (The slash command is /case remove.)

liftedEarly.text: A ban, mute or warning that ended before its time: staff used Unban, Unmute or Remove warn, or accepted an appeal.

warningStage.text: Where a member is on the warn ladder: stage 0 of 3 (no warning ban yet), 1 of 3 (7-day ban), 2 of 3 (30-day ban), 3 of 3 (permanent ban). It does not go back by itself.

canTheyAppeal.text: Whether the member may ask staff to lift a punishment. Yes for almost everything. No for a severe ban that staff marked so, and for a stage 3 ban after 6 months or after a denied appeal.

whatStaffUsuallyGaveForThisReason.term: What staff usually gave for this reason
whatStaffUsuallyGaveForThisReason.text: A hint next to a punishment: what staff gave for the same reason in the last 180 days, so members get similar punishments for similar things.

recordSoFar.text: A member's counted warnings, warning stage, active punishments and appeals, shown on their member page. Members see their own with the "My record" button on the appeal panel.

extraWatchPeriodAfterABan.text: For 7 days after a member comes back from a ban, automod is stricter with them: it starts one punishment step higher, with no friendly notice and no trusted-member leniency. (The slash command is /automod extrawatch.)

warnPrivatelyFirst2MinToFix.term: Warn privately first (2 min to fix)
warnPrivatelyFirst2MinToFix.text: For small automod rules: the first time in 30 days, the member gets a private message and 2 minutes to edit or delete the message. If they fix it, nothing else happens.

friendlyNoticeForAFirstSmallOffence.term: Friendly notice for a first small offence
friendlyNoticeForAFirstSmallOffence.text: A member's first small slip in 30 days (caps, odd characters, English only, mild language) gets a short notice instead of a warning.

reportOnlyDonTDelete.text: An automod mode: staff get a review card about the message, but nothing is deleted and nobody is punished until staff apply it. Good for trying a rule out.

keepApart.text: Staff ask two members to leave each other alone until a set time. Mentions and replies between them are removed. It is not a punishment and does not count as a warning.

safetyLimitTooManyBansOrKicksIn10Minutes.term: Safety limit: too many bans or kicks in 10 minutes
safetyLimitTooManyBansOrKicksIn10Minutes.text: By default, if one moderator bans or kicks more than 5 members in 10 minutes (mutes: 10), Mewvo stops them for an hour and tells the bot owner. Owners can change these numbers. It protects the server if a moderator account is misused.

showWhatChanged.text: A button on a staff alert after many channels or roles were deleted: it compares the last server backup with the server now, so you can put things back with /backup revert.

ticket.text: A private channel where one member talks with staff, opened with a button.

modmail.text: A member sends Mewvo a DM, and staff answer it in a private channel. Mewvo passes the messages back and forth.

supportServer.text: A second, small server where banned members can still appeal, since they cannot see the server they were banned from.

inbox.text: This dashboard's list of everything waiting for staff: appeals, tickets, modmail and automod reviews.

xpAndLevels.text: Members earn points (XP) for chatting. Enough XP is a new level, and levels can give roles.

reactionRoles.text: A message with buttons or a menu where members pick roles for themselves, like "Gamer" or "News".

verification.text: New members press a button to show they are a real person before they can chat.

plan.text: Mewvo is free. Paid plans (Normal, Pro, Max) raise some limits. The server owner's plan counts for the server.

setup.changeOnPage: You can change it on its page.
setup.ownPage: Not set up yet. This one has a few settings, so it opens its own page.
setup.pickHere: Not set up yet. Pick it here and save.
setup.moreSettings: More settings for this: [open its page]({href}).
setup.unreadable: The setup steps could not be loaded just now. Reload the page in a minute.
setup.progress: {done} of {total} essentials done. Go through them in order; the optional steps come after them, skip any you do not need. You can come back here at any time from the sidebar.
setup.rolePosition: Discord lets Mewvo moderate only members whose top role is below Mewvo's own role. In Server Settings → Roles, drag Mewvo's role above your members' roles; roles of admins may stay above it. The count uses the members Mewvo has seen recently, and leaves out admins, bots and the server owner.
